core_job: Today, Radio Tune is a working general Radio Browser and podcast player with nothing distinct in it. Its 4.3(b) clones are TuneIn, myTuner, Simple Radio and radio.net, all checked through the iTunes Search API. The spec repositions it for adults learning a second language by ear. One tap puts live native talk or news radio in the target language in their ears, and the app keeps an honest count of it. Today lists stations on air now in that language, from the exact-language Radio Browser query curl-verified on 2026-10-12. It also shows music and podcasts from the Apple chart of a matching storefront. A 'Just listening' mode keeps the whole world-radio player for everyone else. Everything radiotune owns keeps working: background playback, sleep timer, wake to radio, car mode, favourites, playlists and podcasts.
signature: Immersion Log. Listening time is counted on the device from player events, and only while audio is really playing. It is credited per language, using Radio Browser languagecodes for stations and the RSS <language> tag for episodes, with a manual per-show override when the tag is missing. It is split into talk/news vs music using station tags, and the listener can correct that per station. The Log tab shows a daily goal ring, a streak, a 7-day chart, hours per language and a searchable, filterable session list with CSV export. No other app in the App Store descriptions I checked (iTunes Search API, 2026-10-12) combines live radio by language with listening-time tracking. PolyPod (5 ratings) tracks podcasts only. The radio apps' descriptions have 0 goal/streak/listening-time matches. I did not test the apps themselves, so that claim rests only on their descriptions. Web search was blocked in this session.
